article_content: This year has introduced us to selfies, belfies, and bookshelfies, but now it's time for the 'pelfie' – that's a pet dressed as an elf. Devoted dog and cat owners submitted photos of their four-legged friends in festive attire for a Pet Elfie competition, and the results were adorable. From terriers in elf jackets to a lizard in a tiny red hat, Britain's pets make perfect Santa's little helpers. Sweet-natured Honey the Jack Russell won the BuyAGift 'pet elfie' competition. Her owner, Caroline Virgo, received a £250 voucher and made a £250 charity donation to a dog rescue of her choice. Some pets didn't seem too thrilled about their costumes, like these two dogs dressed as Father Christmas and his reindeer. BuyAGift.com offered a £250 gift voucher and a £250 charity donation for the best entries, and pet lovers across Britain participated enthusiastically. Some even dressed their animals as Father Christmas on his sleigh with a reindeer. The prize ultimately went to Honey, the adorable Jack Russell. Honey's owner, Caroline Virgo, shared, 'Honey loves attention and is very placid. She doesn't mind wearing elf outfits, especially since she wears jumpers during cold walks.' Virgo was thrilled with the win, especially since her husband had recently been in an accident. The prize will allow them to enjoy a relaxing weekend away. Virgo chose Forest Dog Rescue - Green Gap Kennels in Worcestershire for her charity donation, a small rescue center caring for abandoned dogs. While Honey was the overall winner, many other pet owners showcased their creativity. Highlights included a labrador dressed as a snowman and a collie in an elf suit. One impressive feat was dressing a long-haired cat in a full Santa suit. Even a lizard joined the fun with a tiny hat. The competition brought joy and supported a good cause, making it a memorable event for all involved.

article_content: By Associated Press. A Texas man was indicted Thursday for capital murder in a childhood attack on a boy who died nearly 13 years later from skin cancer blamed on the horrific burns he suffered in the assault. Authorities allege that at age 13, Don Willburn Collins attacked Robert Middleton on his eighth birthday in 1998 near the younger boy's home in Splendora, about 35 miles northeast of Houston. Middleton was burned across 99 percent of his body and endured years of physical therapy before he died in 2011. The grand jury's indictment Thursday came after a judge ruled in March that Collins' case could be transferred from juvenile to adult court. Charged: Don Willburn Collins was indicted Thursday for capital murder in a childhood attack on a boy who died nearly 13 years later from skin cancer blamed on the horrific burns he suffered in the assault. Maimed: Middleton was burned on his eighth birthday, and shortly before his death gave a videotaped deposition accusing Collins of sexually assaulting him two weeks before the attack. Middleton had initially named Collins as his attacker and the older boy was arrested in 1998. Collins spent several months in juvenile detention but was released after prosecutors said they did not have enough evidence to pursue the case. Shortly before he died, Middleton gave a videotaped deposition in which he accused Collins for the first time of sexually assaulting him two weeks before the attack. Held: Middleton had initially named Collins as his attacker and the older boy was arrested in 1998. The sexual assault allegation prompted investigators to reopen the case, and prosecutors charged the now 28-year-old Collins with murder last year — but they needed to move the case from juvenile to adult court to take him to trial. Colleen Middleton, Robert's mother, said she was relieved the case would go to trial. 'When Robert died we were thinking maybe nothing will ever happen, maybe someone is just going to get away with what they did to him,' she said. 'It's been a long road.' Montgomery County District Attorney Brett Ligon said he hopes the case can be tried by the end of the year. Horror injuries: Attacked on his eighth birthday, Robert Middleton was burned across 99 percent of his body and endured years of physical therapy before he died in 2011. Several witnesses testified that Collins had confessed to them or others that he had been responsible for the attack on Middleton. But E. Tay Bond, an attorney for Collins, now 29, said there is no credible evidence in the case that would result in a conviction. 'I think the indictment for capital murder is a direct reflection of the desire that this community has to hold someone accountable for the tragedy that was bestowed upon Mr. Middleton,' Bond said. Collins, who is being held on $1 million bond, is set to be arraigned on June 19. Bond said he plans to ask for a change of venue and will present evidence at trial of Collins' history of mental disability. One point of contention is the maximum prison sentence Collins could face if convicted. If Collins had been certified to stand trial as an adult when he was a juvenile, his maximum sentence would have been 40 years. The maximum term for capital murder as an adult is life in prison. 'We believe the full range of punishment is life,' Ligon said. Bond said 40 years should be the maximum possible sentence. Collins also faces a charge in neighboring San Jacinto County of failing to register as a sex offender.

article_content: Lawrence Russell Brewer was executed in Texas on Wednesday evening for his role in the infamous 1998 dragging death of James Byrd, a black man. Brewer, 44, was one of three men convicted for their involvement in Byrd's murder. The execution took place at 6:21 p.m. local time via lethal injection, according to the Texas Department of Criminal Justice. Prior to his execution, Brewer had an extensive final meal. As reported by Jason Clark, a spokesperson for the Texas Department of Criminal Justice, Brewer's meal included chicken fried steaks, a triple-meat bacon cheeseburger, a cheese omelet, fried okra, barbecue, fajitas, pizza, and peanut butter fudge with crushed peanuts. After his meal, Brewer was given time to make phone calls to his family and friends. On the night of June 7, 1998, Brewer, along with two other white men, kidnapped the 49-year-old Byrd. They chained him by the ankles to the back of a pickup truck and dragged him for over three miles down a rural road near Jasper, Texas. Byrd died after being decapitated when he hit a culvert. Prosecutors described the crime as one of the most brutal hate crimes in U.S. history, aimed at promoting Brewer's fledgling white supremacist organization. During his 1999 trial, prosecutors portrayed Brewer as a racist psychopath. Brewer, a former 'Exalted Cyclops' of a racist prison gang affiliated with the Ku Klux Klan, had spent most of his adult life in prison for various crimes. Brewer testified that he was a bystander, not a killer, tearfully admitting his presence during Byrd's dragging but denying any intent to cause harm. He blamed John William King for starting the attack and Shawn Berry for slashing Byrd's throat and chaining him to the truck. Brewer admitted to kicking Byrd and spraying his face with black paint, actions he claimed were reflexive attempts to stop the fight. When Brewer was sentenced to death in 1999, Jasper County District Attorney Guy James Gray stated that the death penalty was necessary in Brewer's case to prevent future violence. The jury's decision was based on their unanimous agreement that Brewer posed a future threat to society, intended to kill Byrd, and that there were no mitigating circumstances to spare his life. Brewer's execution was the 11th in Texas this year. His accomplice, John William King, also received a death sentence and is awaiting the outcome of an appeal. Shawn Berry was sentenced to life in prison. In 2009, President Barack Obama signed into law expanded hate crime legislation named after James Byrd and Matthew Shepard, a gay man who died after being severely beaten in 1998.

article_content: By Iona Kirby and Jade Watkins. PUBLISHED: 02:41 EST, 10 December 2012 | UPDATED: 02:42 EST, 10 December 2012 She was rushed to the hospital on Friday morning after what was first suspected to be an overdose but later diagnosed as 'exhaustion and dehydration'. Just two days later, Brooke Mueller appeared determined to get back to normal and looked happy and relaxed as she took her twin sons to a friend's wedding in Los Angeles. The smiling 35-year-old, who has a history of drug abuse, escorted the three-year-old boys to the ceremony and helped them scatter flowers along the wedding walkway. Drama over: Brooke Mueller appeared smiling at a Los Angeles wedding as she helped twin sons Bob and Max scatter flowers down the wedding walkway on Sunday. The ex-wife of Charlie Sheen wore a pair of loose-fitting black trousers and a slinky grey shawl, while sons Bob and Max looked smart in white suits. The outing comes just two days after Mueller was rushed to the hospital in what was initially thought to be an overdose. However, Mueller's publicist, Steve Honig, spoke out to claim that no drugs were involved. Instead, Honig said in a statement that Brooke was mistakenly believed to be unresponsive while sleeping, telling MailOnline: 'An assistant thought Brooke was non-responsive while she was napping and hastily called an ambulance.' 'As a precaution, Brooke was brought to a local hospital and discharged after an hour. She was diagnosed with exhaustion and dehydration and is now fine and resting at home. That's it.' But in a video posted on TMZ, Brooke was seen leaving the hospital after being discharged with blackened hands, leading to speculation that she had been using crack cocaine and burnt herself. But the socialite claimed that her hands were in fact covered in spray paint from an art project. The troubled mother-of-two also blamed her exhaustion on a line of jewelry making she’s been working on for her new boyfriend, jeweler Pascal Mouawad, with whom she was having dinner at Mr. Chow's the night before the incident. 'See? Look,' she said, clutching a wad of trinkets with mysteriously blackened fingertips. 'Jewelry. Everywhere is jewelry.' The previous evening she was seen looking glassy-eyed as she stepped out of a car upon her arrival at the Beverly Hills restaurant. Sources reportedly told the website that people around Brooke are 'deeply concerned' and alleged that she had been 'taking drugs for several weeks', it was claimed. More trouble: Brooke, pictured on Thursday evening, was rushed to the hospital on Friday morning. The morning after the night before: The previous evening Brooke was seen arriving for dinner at Mr. Chow restaurant. Rocky relationship: Brooke is best-known for her marriage to Charlie Sheen, pictured in 2009. But Brooke is so determined to prove she was clean, she told Radar Online: 'I am going back to the hospital to get the test results that will prove that I wasn't on drugs.' For her meal out on Thursday night, Brooke went for a boho look, sporting a jeweled headband and a leather jacket, trousers, and studded boots. Meanwhile, it was reported that the toddlers were in the care of Mueller's live-in nanny during her hospital dash. Sources told TMZ that the caretaker looked after the tots during the former real estate agent's absence. The boys stayed at Mueller's house with the nanny, who has lived in the household for several years, and did not go to their father Sheen's house nor were put under the care of the actor's other ex-wife Denise Richards, who has looked after them in the past. Brooke was placed on probation for one year after she pleaded guilty to possession of cocaine on March 19. The Witchouse actress and mother-of-two has been in rehab multiple times. Brooke married Charlie Sheen in May 2008 and gave birth to their twin sons Bob and Max nine months later. Charlie filed for divorce from Brooke in November 2010, and the pair's divorce became effective the following June.

article_content: From rare gadgets to leftover cheese sandwiches, eBay has it all. As the UK site marks its 15th anniversary, three clever sellers share how it made them millionaires. Mark Radcliffe, Anthony Ponsford, and Alison Abruneiras are among thousands of British eBay millionaires who struck gold on the platform. Mark Radcliffe became the first British eBay millionaire by starting First2Save in 1999 from his parents' garden shed. Alison Abruneiras and Anthony Ponsford also surpassed the £1 million mark by dealing with independent retailers online. By offering sought-after items at fixed prices, these entrepreneurs joined millions of online stores that shifted eBay from an auction site to a bustling marketplace. Mark Radcliffe, a former Tesco employee from Stockport, Manchester, invested £200 from his earnings to launch First2Save, specializing in mobile phones and tech accessories. Fifteen years later, he credits eBay for his success. 'I could have stayed at Tesco and become a manager, but it wouldn't have challenged me. I still can't believe it—it's a dream come true,' he told the Sun. On his company's 10th anniversary, Radcliffe emphasized the importance of knowledge and support. 'I couldn't have done it without the right people and staying updated with technology,' he said. Mrs. Abruneiras, a mother of three with no formal qualifications, started her eBay journey to cope with her cancer diagnosis. Her daughter now helps run the eBay shop, while she manages a tapas restaurant with her husband. Anthony Ponsford left his city lawyer job to start Piranha Trading Limited, selling items like camera memory cards and pet furniture from China. Describing himself as a real-life Del Boy, Ponsford said, 'I often joke that I've created an online version of Trotter's Independent Traders.' Despite initial struggles and the 2008 recession, his business thrived. 'Strangely, the recession helped because people sought bargains online,' he noted. Alison Abruneiras launched her eBay shop, Nail and Beauty Emporium, which now trades globally. 'It's incredible to think this started at my computer,' she said. 'It's been hard work, but if I can do it, anyone can.' eBay has evolved significantly since its launch in 1995 by Pierre Omidyar. Today, ebay.co.uk boasts over 19 million monthly users and has traded £65 billion worth of goods. 'Shoppers' expectations have changed dramatically,' said Tanya Lawler, eBay's UK Vice President. 'The UK will spend £45 billion shopping online this year, and eBay's evolution reflects Britain's retail transformation.'

article_content: Police in North Carolina claim to have evidence showing that Jesus Huerta, a 17-year-old Latino teen, fatally shot himself while handcuffed in the back of a police vehicle. The preliminary findings of their internal investigation, released today, clear the officers of any misconduct. The autopsy report confirms that Huerta died from a close-range gunshot wound to the face. During a press conference, authorities stated that gunpowder residue was found on a glove worn by Huerta, but not on the arresting officer's hand. They also mentioned that no weapon was discovered during a routine check of the police car at the start of the officer's shift. Huerta's family remains unconvinced and has renewed their call for a federal investigation. 'Is this the kind of police culture we want? The culture starts at the top, with the chief,' said family attorney Alex Charns. On November 19, Huerta's sister reported him missing. Police located him around 2:30 a.m. and found he had an outstanding warrant for trespassing. Officer Sam Duncan arrested Huerta, handcuffed him, and placed him in the patrol car after a pat-down that did not detect a gun. Police claim Huerta shot himself en route to the station. The controversial case has led to multiple protests. In one instance, police used tear gas to disperse a crowd that had gathered in downtown Durham. Another vigil for Huerta turned violent when police in riot gear used tear gas and batons to disperse the crowd. Police Chief Jose Lopez defended his officers' actions, stating, 'I could not be more proud of the restraint and professionalism demonstrated by our officers.'

article_content: Elite private institutions are progressively abandoning GCSEs in favor of the more demanding International GCSEs (IGCSEs), which are reminiscent of the old O-levels. These schools view IGCSEs as superior preparation for A-levels, despite recent government overhauls of standard exams. The shift is evident in the 18% surge in IGCSE entries this summer, totaling 152,170, which constitutes 38.7% of all Year 11 exam entries in independent schools. Conversely, GCSE entries dropped from 274,183 to 242,181. Over 400 schools affiliated with the Independent Schools Council (ISC) had students taking at least one IGCSE.
